title: 登金陵凤凰台
author: 李白
intro: Standing on an old terrace in Nanjing, Li Bai sees that the phoenixes and the kingdoms are gone while the river flows on — and, looking towards the capital, feels the sting of his own exile from court.
analysis: 金陵就是今天的南京，三国的吴和东晋都曾在这里建都。传说南朝时有凤凰飞来，人们就修了凤凰台。诗一开头连用三个“凤”字：凤凰台上曾经有凤凰游玩，现在凤凰飞走了，台也空了，只有长江还在自己流——繁华会消失，自然却永恒。第二联怀古：吴国宫殿的花草埋没了小路，东晋的达官贵人也都变成了古老的坟墓。第三联转写眼前的大景：三座山一半隐在青天外，江水被白鹭洲分成两道。最后一联最重要：总是因为浮云能遮住太阳，看不见长安，让人发愁——“浮云蔽日”比喻小人蒙蔽皇帝，李白是在说自己被排挤出朝廷。全诗从怀古写到现实，从风景写到心事，气势开阔，被认为可以和崔颢的《黄鹤楼》相比。
analysisEn: Jinling is today’s Nanjing, once the capital of the Wu kingdom and the Eastern Jin. Legend says phoenixes gathered here in the fifth century, so a terrace was built to mark the omen. The opening line uses “phoenix” three times in quick succession: phoenixes once played on Phoenix Terrace; now they are gone, the terrace is empty, and only the river flows on by itself. Glory disappears; nature stays. The second couplet looks back: flowers and grass of the Wu palace have buried its paths, and the grand nobles of Jin are now just old burial mounds. The third couplet turns to the huge view before him — three peaks half lost beyond the blue sky, the river split in two by White Egret Isle. The final couplet carries the real weight: “it’s always because drifting clouds can hide the sun that I cannot see Chang’an, and I grieve.” Clouds blocking the sun was a standard image for bad officials blinding the emperor; Li Bai, recently pushed out of court, is talking about himself. The poem moves from history to the present and from scenery to heartache, and is often compared with Cui Hao’s “Yellow Crane Tower”, which it seems to answer.
background: Li Bai (701–762) left the court in Chang’an around 744 after being slandered by powerful courtiers, and spent years wandering the lower Yangtze. This poem was probably written during a visit to Jinling in that period; it is traditionally said he wrote it to rival Cui Hao’s famous poem.
pronunciation: 总为 wèi（因为）；鹭 lù。机器朗读“总为”容易读成 wéi，已在朗读用字中替换同音字。
version: 采用通行文本。重要异文：“二水中分白鹭洲”一作“一水中分白鹭洲”；“吴宫花草”一作“吴宫芳草”。网站用通行的“二水”“花草”。

lines.py: fèng huáng tái shàng fèng huáng yóu
lines.lit: On Phoenix Terrace phoenixes once roamed;
lines.en: Once phoenixes played on Phoenix Terrace;

lines.py: fèng qù tái kōng jiāng zì liú
lines.lit: the phoenixes gone, the terrace empty, the river flows on by itself.
lines.en: now they are gone, the terrace stands empty, and the river just flows on.

lines.py: wú gōng huā cǎo mái yōu jìng
lines.lit: The flowers and grass of the Wu palace bury its secluded paths;
lines.en: Weeds and flowers have swallowed the paths of the Wu palace,

lines.py: jìn dài yī guān chéng gǔ qiū
lines.lit: the robed and capped nobles of Jin have become ancient mounds.
lines.en: and the fine lords of Jin are only old grave mounds.

lines.py: sān shān bàn luò qīng tiān wài
lines.lit: The Three Peaks half drop beyond the blue sky;
lines.en: Three peaks fade, half hidden, at the edge of the blue sky;

lines.py: èr shuǐ zhōng fēn bái lù zhōu
lines.lit: two streams are split in the middle by White Egret Isle.
lines.en: White Egret Isle splits the river into two.

lines.py: zǒng wèi fú yún néng bì rì
lines.lit: It is all because drifting clouds can hide the sun
lines.en: Always the drifting clouds come and cover the sun —

lines.py: cháng ān bù jiàn shǐ rén chóu
lines.lit: that Chang’an cannot be seen, which makes one grieve.
lines.en: I cannot see Chang’an, and my heart is heavy.

words.en: phoenix, a bird of good omen
words.note: 现代汉语仍用；凤凰出现被看作太平吉祥的征兆。

words.en: the palace of the Wu kingdom (3rd century)
words.note: 三国时孙权在金陵建都。
书面语。现代汉语“小径”“曲径通幽”。

words.en: robes and caps — i.e. nobles and officials
words.note: 现代汉语“衣冠整齐”；成语“衣冠楚楚”。

words.en: Three Peaks, a hill southwest of Nanjing
words.note: 在南京西南长江边，有三座山峰相连。
古时长江中的沙洲，今已和陆地相连。
比喻小人蒙蔽君主，今天也作成语用。
使：让。现代汉语多说“让人发愁”。

imagery.name: 凤
imagery.zh: 凤凰曾来象征过去的繁荣吉祥，凤凰飞走表示那个时代一去不返。
imagery.en: The phoenixes’ visit stood for a glorious, lucky past; their leaving means that age is gone for good.

imagery.name: 台
imagery.zh: 空荡荡的凤凰台是历史变迁的见证，也是诗人登高远望、抒发感慨的地方。
imagery.en: The empty terrace witnesses history’s changes and is where the poet stands, looking far and brooding.

imagery.name: 江
imagery.zh: 长江“自流”，不管朝代兴亡，象征自然的永恒和人事的短暂。
imagery.en: The Yangtze flows on “by itself”, careless of rising and falling dynasties — nature lasts, human glory doesn’t.

imagery.name: 云
imagery.zh: 遮住太阳的浮云，比喻朝中排挤他的小人。
imagery.en: Drifting clouds blocking the sun stand for the scheming courtiers who pushed him away from the emperor.
